analysis:
Both changed files are in the ProviderBenchmark module: SchedulerPrefillBenchmark.swift and SchedulerPrefillDecisionLiveRunner.swift. They are benchmark and measurement tooling, not the serving path. Nothing in them touches the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), key custody (A-002, A-003), attestation (TB-009, TB-011), the fan helper (TB-010), or SSD cache storage and crypto (T-041).

SchedulerPrefillBenchmark.swift (head lines 17-19, 47-54, 131-142, 209-211): the report schema goes from version 4 to 5. It adds optional fields prefillChunkTokens and maxBatchedTokensPerStep, taken from EngineV2Factory.prefillGeometry(model:). These are numeric geometry values, not prompt content, key material or identities, so the report discloses nothing new. The new optional fields are backward-compatible. Any gate that consumes the report must reject or handle schema 5 and absent fields explicitly. That is a measurement-integrity question rather than a security one, and the consumer is not in the supplied evidence.

SchedulerPrefillDecisionLiveRunner.swift (head lines 64-80, 101-102): the environment overrides for the benchmark engine are factored into engineEnvironment. It now also sets the prefill chunk key and the step token budget key, alongside the existing max-partial-prefills and solo-stripe keys. The overrides apply to a local copy of the environment dictionary passed to makeProductionBuild with constructionPurpose .benchmark. The process environment is not mutated, and no production serving engine is affected. The values come from the simulated Configuration, so they are not attacker-controlled input over the wire.

Not visible: the implementations of EngineV2Factory.prefillGeometry, prefillChunkKey and stepTokenBudgetKey, and the validation of Configuration values. Out-of-range values would be a local benchmark robustness issue, not a threat-model regression. Prompts are synthetic tiled tokens, so no consumer plaintext (A-001) is involved.

No findings.
